name: Pork Chops au Poivre (Creamy Peppercorn Sauce)

fit.evidence: 515 cal is inside the 400-650 band; 4g carbs is well under the 35g ceiling; seared pork chop with a pan sauce, no rice/potato/pasta/bread base; scales to 14 via sear-and-weigh-divide in a skillet; no seafood.

catalog_check: No catalog pork dish shares the au poivre flavor family. Nearest live catalog chops are creamy-mushroom-pork-chops-over-mashed-potatoes (mushroom cream + mashed-potato base), marry-me-pork-chops-over-pasta (sun-dried-tomato cream over pasta), countryfried-pork-chops-with-bacon-gravy (breaded + bacon gravy), and pork-tenderloin-stroganoff-over-egg-noodles (sour-cream mushroom, tenderloin + noodles) - all differ in sauce family and all carry a starch base this one lacks. Nothing in the 118-recipe pork catalog is a peppercorn/brandy/beef-broth cream pan sauce.

borderline.where: accepted-slugs.json (in-run accept, not yet in catalog digest)
borderline.reason: 3-of-4 structural match: same protein (pork chop), same starch (none), same method (skillet sear + creamy alcohol-deglazed pan sauce). The differing axis is the sauce/flavor family - au poivre's cracked-peppercorn + brandy + beef-broth cream vs the accepted dish's garlic-herb-white-wine cream. Au poivre is a named, iconic French preparation whose peppercorn-brandy signature genuinely distinguishes the plate (paprikash-vs-goulash logic), so I rule KEEP - but the 'creamy skillet pork chop' slot is now doubling up, so I flag it for the decider to make the final catalog-fit call rather than silently seat two.

cross_protein_twins: Steak au poivre (BEEF) is the classic canonical form of this exact dish - a beef selector may hold a structurally identical peppercorn-brandy-cream seared-steak candidate; flag for the orchestrator's cross-protein merge.
Any 'creamy peppercorn chicken' or 'creamy peppercorn turkey' cutlet in the chicken/turkey pools would be the same dinner on a different protein - same sauce, same method, no starch.
pricer_flags: shallot (may map to onion or need new commodity)
notes: Candidate's own 'why' references a pool candidate 'peppercorn-crusted-pork-rib-chops' (dry cracked-pepper crust, no cream) - that is a pool item, not in the live catalog, and is a genuinely different dish (crust vs cream sauce), so not a catalog dupe. Left-in unmapped ingredients are intentional per the pricer-lane exercise and were not penalized.
